newsitem.title: UK: Shipper short covering supports new crop UK grains.
newsitem.headline: Shipper short covering supports new crop UK grains.

text.p: New crop wheat staged a slight rally on the UK cash and futures grain markets on Tuesday as brokers reported good interest from shippers for it, while old crop interest appears to have faded.
"We have seen good short covering from shippers today and there is also a feeling that new crop has gone down enough," said one broker.
On the cash markets only one trade was reported for fob feed wheat at 92.25 stg a tonne for November ex-east coast ports.
Delivered feed wheat was fetching between 92 and 93 stg a tonne for Oct/Dec material, depending on area, while June was trading at 86 stg across the country.
New crop barley fetched 85.50 stg for harvest in East Anglia while material in the New Year was trading at 85 stg.
There was no milling wheat business reported.
On the LIFFE wheat futures market old crop July was 0.50 stg down while new crop was 0.50 to 0.15 stg up on a total turnover of 335 lots.
Most active November traded 194 lots before closing 0.50 stg up.
LIFFE barley futures continued to drift lower with traded levels 0.25 to 0.50 stg down on the day after trading 43 lots.
